title: The Tyranny of the Alphabet 2
contentHtml:
I wrote about the Tyranny of the Alphabet many years ago. In economics the standard then was to list authors alphabetically:

Faculty members in top departments with surnames beginning with letters earlier in the alphabet are substantially more likely to be tenured, be fellows of the Econometric Society, and even win Nobel prizes (let’s see, Arrow, Buchanan, Coase…hmmm). No such effects are found in psychology where the alphabetical norm is not followed.

The tyranny is still with us. The AEA now lets coauthors certify a random order with the ⓡ symbol, as in Ray ⓡ Robson, but alphabetical order remains the norm.

Chris Dalla Riva has a nice example of alphabetical tyranny from the Grammys. From 2021 to 2025 the Grammys basically listed nominees alphabetically (the details are a bit messy see Dalla Riva for the full story), and lo and behold nominees with starting names beginning with A,B,C, D or E won suspiciously more than one would expect compared to the share of such names in the Billboard charts.
